summary: Rabbi Besser explores the spiritual significance of the three weeks leading up to Tish'a BeAb, focusing on the power of vision and the dangers of Lashon Hara. He discusses the story of the spies in Parashat Debarim to illustrate how negative speech and lack of empathy can lead to destruction, while emphasizing the importance of sensitivity toward others.
questions: What is the spiritual significance of the three weeks before Tish'a BeAb?
Why did Moshe Rabbenu change Hoshea's name to Yehoshua?
How does Lashon Hara relate to the destruction of the Bet HaMikdash?
What does it mean to have the vision of Sarah Abinu?
How can we use our personal challenges to develop empathy for others?
